LHX.sentence: L3Harris has fallen a long way — it's down about 37% from its high and sitting right near its lowest point of the year — but nothing has changed about steady military demand, so it looks unusually cheap for a defense company right now.

ASML.sentence: ASML had a nice up week, and while its price looks eye-wateringly expensive on paper, that's mostly because their earnings are about to jump — this is still the only company in the world making a certain essential chipmaking machine.

LIN.sentence: Linde is quiet, but interestingly it's trading no richer than its rivals despite usually commanding a premium for being the best in the business — the industrial gas story of steady demand and small regular price increases just keeps ticking along.

MSFT.sentence: Microsoft slipped a touch and has lagged its big-tech peers over the past month, but the AI cloud story keeps grinding along without any real drama.

TMO.sentence: Thermo Fisher is calm, and there's a good sign underneath — biotech funding has thawed sharply, and when the money flows to labs, orders for Thermo's equipment tend to follow a couple of quarters later.

ENB.sentence: Enbridge is calm — this pipeline toll-road business pays a solid dividend, though at today's price it's fairly valued rather than a genuine bargain.

NOW.sentence: ServiceNow dropped a bit this week and is now well off its high, even as big companies and government agencies keep signing on for its AI workflow tools — those are long, sticky contracts, so this looks like a rare discount on a strong grower.

GLNCY.sentence: Glencore had a nice day and actually held up better than copper prices did, which shows the value of its trading arm making money even when the metals themselves wobble.

MLM.sentence: Martin Marietta ticked up, and the number that really matters kept improving — the price it gets per ton of crushed stone is rising faster than its costs, proof that each quarry still quietly owns its own patch of the map.

KOF.sentence: Coca-Cola FEMSA drifted down slightly with a softer Mexican peso, which matters since most of its earnings are in pesos, but there's nothing unusual happening in the business.

PBR.A.sentence: Petrobras had a good day with oil prices sitting high, which is a direct boost to this Brazilian oil company known for paying out big dividends when crude cooperates.

AMKBY.sentence: Maersk, the Danish container-shipping giant, slipped a bit, but the whole company is currently priced below what its fleet of ships would actually cost to replace — an unusually cheap starting point for a business tied to global trade.

MA.sentence: Mastercard barely moved and is trading no higher than Visa even though it usually commands a premium — people keep tapping their cards more than ever, so there's nothing wrong with the business, just an unusually flat patch.

ISRG.sentence: The da Vinci surgical robot maker had a strong day and is well off its high even though hospitals keep doing more procedures on its machines — and every operation means more disposable instruments sold, which is where most of its money comes from.
